transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-17 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Verdant - Head of Data), Samir Patel (Verdant - Platform Lead), Ellen Wu (Verdant - Procurement)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and how Redwood surfaces per-route cost breakdowns; discuss cost-saving levers (batching, caching, quantization) and pilot/benchmark next steps.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Marta: good thanks, excited to see the console, we — we've been looking at cost numbers and want to understand per-route attribution.
00:15 Priya: great, I'll share my screen now, give me one sec, and i'll open the Redwood Console, um — apologies if the initial load is a bit slow, network at my end.
00:30 Priya: ok so top left is the account overview, token usage over time, you can filter by model, route, and date range. You mentioned wanting per-route, so i'll jump to Routes.
01:05 Priya: here we have per-route dashboards — each route shows throughput, p50/p95 latency, tokens in vs tokens out, and importantly a per-route cost column which breaks down compute vs model vs caching.
01:30 Marta: can we see cost allocated to multi-turn chat vs single-turn embedding calls? that's what's driving our spend right now.
01:40 Priya: yes, routes are arbitrary — you define them in the API or via our SDK and we attribute by route id. so you'll get separate lines for chat-agent, web-search-embed, etc. you can also tag routes with product-owner metadata.
02:10 Jordan: often customers want token-level cost for a journey, so our cost breakdown shows per-token compute cost, plus any storage (kv cache) amortization. note these are estimates tied to your committed capacity and the model profile.
02:35 Samir: quick q — how accurate are these numbers vs our cloud billing? we need them to tie back to internal chargeback.
02:45 Priya: good question — the console uses an internal unit-cost model that maps to GPU-hour and token accounting; we provide a CSV export so you can reconcile with actual cloud bills. it's not a perfect 1:1 if you're on shared hosted plan vs dedicated; if you go Dedicated we can calibrate the model to your reserved capacity numbers.
03:20 Marta: nice. that export — does it include per-request metadata so we can join to our logs?
03:28 Priya: yes we include request_id, route_id, model_variant, timestamp, token_in, token_out, approx_cost_usd. privacy note: payloads are not included in the export unless you enable that option with consent.
03:45 Ellen: from procurement — curious about discounts for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go; also need SOC2 artifact and SSO details.
03:55 Jordan: we have reserved capacity pricing and a midpoint estimate in the pricing sheet; i'll send the tailored pricing scenarios. for compliance, Priya will drop the SOC2 and network diagrams.
04:20 Priya: jumping back to the console, this panel is usage heatmaps by hour — helpful to size autoscaling and burst policies. customers use this to set autoscale windows to avoid overprovisioning.
04:45 Priya: here's the per-model performance profile (auto-collected) — p50/p95 latencies per sequence length. that helps choose model variants per route.
05:10 Samir: we have a lot of short requests (search/faq), want to keep p50 under 120ms and minimize cost. suggestions?
05:20 Priya: tend to recommend 1) use smaller model variant for short queries (redwood-compact or quantized variants), 2) enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, 3) batching for background/async routes. Console shows cost impact if you toggle those settings.
05:45 Marta: can you show the simulated cost delta if we switch chat-agent to a quantized 8-bit variant?
05:52 Priya: yes — there's a scenario tool, open Scenarios -> Route Optimization. i'll pick chat-agent, switch to q8 variant, keep same throughput, and it projects ~42% token compute savings but slight p95 latency increase in heavy tail. note transcription: the numbers are... um.. approximations, we usually run a benchmark to confirm.
06:25 Jordan: that's where Redwood Optimize recommendations come in — automated suggestions for batching, quantization, and suggested route-level model pinning. we can run an eval on your traffic sample to project savings more precisely.
06:45 Samir: for the pilot, we can provide sample traffic for 24 hours. how long for benchmarking?
06:50 Priya: we can run a targeted benchmark in 48 hours after getting the sample, results + tuned config in 3 business days.
07:05 Marta: in terms of routing/fallbacks, if we pin to a quantized variant and it breaches latency SLO, will requests fail?
07:12 Priya: no — we have smart routing and fallback policies. you can set per-route fallbacks to a higher-capacity model or dedicated pool; console will show failover rates in the dashboard.
07:28 Jordan: also auto-rollouts: you can do a canary and the console shows quality/regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
07:40 Samir: about VPC/private deployment — we have sensitive PII in prompts. what are our options?
07:48 Priya: Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is available; for sensitive data customers usually go Dedicated with VPC peering, or full Private if required. we support KMS integrations and audit logs export. we'll share the architecture doc.
08:05 Ellen: procurement: what else do you need from our side to start a pilot? PO? just a signed SOW?
08:12 Jordan: usually a pilot SOW + sample traffic and a short security review. for larger pilots we do a minimal order for Dedicated capacity. we'll align based on the cost scenarios.
08:30 Priya: back to console, you can also create alerting rules on cost-per-route thresholds, and tie alerts to Slack/email; handy to stop runaway jobs.
08:50 Marta: curious about attribution for multi-step workflows — we have a flow where search -> summarization -> action. can we see per-step cost and end-to-end tokens?
09:00 Priya: yes if you instrument each step as a route and pass correlation ids, the console aggregates the end-to-end journey with a trace view. we surface per-step cost and total.
09:25 Samir: any limitations on export frequency? we automate nightly reconciliation.
09:30 Priya: exports can be scheduled nightly; there's also an API for ad-hoc pulls.
09:40 Marta: can we restrict who sees cost data? finance shouldn't see raw prompts.
09:45 Jordan: role-based access controls (RBAC) allow you to limit fields per role; cost analytics are gated to roles you define. SSO/SAML support included.
10:05 Priya: small note — some customers see a delta between console projected cost and cloud bills during pilot because of batch amortization and cold start effects; we monitor and adjust.
10:25 Marta: ok that's fair. let's talk specifics: we currently have ~500k short search requests/day and ~50k multi-turn chats. rough monthly token volume ~4B tokens.
10:40 Jordan: with those numbers, initial estimate is around $Xk/month on hosted, but with reserved capacity and q8 variants for searches we expect 30-45% savings. i'll run a tailored calc and include that in the pricing sheet.
11:00 Samir: on the technical side, we want to run a benchmark for our top 5 routes: search, product-recommend, chat-assist, embedding-index, batch-async. we'll hand over traffic samples.
11:15 Priya: perfect. we'll set up dedicated sandbox with matching model variants and run throughput/latency/cost profile.
11:30 Marta: for the canary and rollout, will the console show quality regressions vs our evaluation prompts?
11:36 Priya: yes — you can upload eval prompt sets and the console will report BLEU/ROUGE/ad-hoc metrics or mismatch rates and trigger alerts if metric drops beyond threshold. it's plumbed into rollouts.
12:00 Jordan: quick recap — Jordan will send pricing + tailored cost model, Priya will send SOC2 and VPC docs, Samir to share traffic samples and desired pilot dates, Ellen to provide procurement timeline. propose pilot week of 2026-05-24.
12:20 Marta: sounds good, thanks both.
12:25 Ellen: noted on procurement, we'll try to have initial PO template ready.
12:32 Jordan: thanks folks, we'll follow up in email with the attachments and calendar invite for the benchmark.

End transcript.
